text.p: Medical Industries of America Inc Monday denied alligations it failed to accurately convert shares under a Regulation S transaction and charged suits claiming failure were brought by "investors who may be short stock to negatively impact the market for our stock."
The company also said it has made dramatic progress in its turnaround efforts.
Medical Industries said it has been informed of a lawsuit brought by a limited number of offshore investors alleging the company's failure to accurately convert shares.
"We have not seen the paperwork, but the allegations referenced in the (report) are totally without merit," chief executive Michael Morrell said.

"We converted these people precisely according to the terms and conditions defined within the subscription documents they signed. We have sought various legal opinions that have all confirmed that the conversion formulas were implemented properly and accurately."
He also said "Our shareholders have been seriously damaged by these investors and we intend to file the necessary counter claims."

Commenting on the turnaround, Morrell said that, "based on the operating success we have enjoyed this past January, we fully anticipate being able to report a major improvement in the first quarter of 1997.

"This is due primarily to the decrease in expenses ($1.35 million in annual G&A), a 23 percent increase in cath lab revenue this January as compared to January of 1996, a 300 percent increase in the number of cath cases from January 1996 to January 1997, the addition of revenue realized from FPII, and an increase in revenue from two Essential Care Clinics."
